question.leadin: This conflict began due to a dispute over whether Native Americans should be driven out of Virginia.
question.text: Name this 1676 rebellion against colonial governor William Berkeley. It collapsed after its namesake died of dysentery.
question.clue: A target of this conflict who owned the Green Spring Plantation was William Berkeley.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions related to the Seven Years' War.
swap.text: The American theater of the Seven Years' War is commonly known by this name, which references the two main enemies that the British colonists fought during the war.
swap.clue: Daniel de Beaujeu ("boh-ZHOH") won this war's Battle of Monongahela ("muh-non-guh-HEE-luh"), where General Braddock died trying to reach Fort Duquesne ("dyoo-KAYN").

question.text: In this 1676 war, which included the Great Swamp Fight, a namesake chief fought soldiers and priests from Plymouth and Massachusetts Bay. Native or colonial name acceptable.
question.answerHtml: King Philip’s War [or Metacomet’s War; or Pometacomet’s War; accept “rebellion” in place of “war”]
question.clue: A turning point in this conflict occurred with the Great Swamp Fight, after which the Narragansett were forced to withdraw.

swap.leadin: This publication predicted the death of Titan Leeds in 1732. Leeds wasn't dead in 1733, but this publication printed an obituary anyway; when Leeds protested, this publication suspected an imposter.
swap.text: Name this annual publication, filled with astronomical information, poems, proverbs, and a calendar, that was extremely popular in the American colonies.
swap.clue: Naval hero John Paul Jones named his ship after this publication.

question.leadin: It was built by Contrecoeur in 1754 to secure the Ohio Valley during the French and Indian War.
question.text: Name this French fort in Pennsylvania which was the target of the Braddock expedition, which turned into a fiasco. Fort Necessity was built to increase British power in the region so that an attack on this fort could occur.
question.clue: This place was part of a series of fortifications including Fort Machault and Fort Le Boeuf.

swap.text: Ivar the Boneless conquered this city, which then became the center of the Danelaw. This city was the birthplace of the scholar Alcuin, who was the head of the palace school at Aachen.
swap.clue: Houses named for Lancashire (LAN-kush-er) and this city were the primary factions in the War of the Roses.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about rebellions in colonial America, none of which were the American Revolution.
question.text: James II consolidated several northern colonies into this entity, led by Joseph Dudley and then Edmund Andros. Colonists revolted against Andros when word of England's Glorious Revolution spread.
question.answer: Dominion of New England in America
question.clue: Its first president later became chief justice of New York, and sentenced Jacob Leisler to death for treason.

swap.leadin: Name some Native American groups outside the Five Nations who spoke Iroquoian languages.
swap.text: This tribe joined the Five Nations in 1722 following their namesake war against the British in North Carolina. This group's addition resulted in the modern-day Iroquois League having six nations.
swap.answerHtml: Tuscarora [accept Skarure; prompt on hemp gatherers or shirt wearers and equivalent]
swap.clue: They threatened to take sides in the struggle between Thomas Cary and Governor Hyde, and ultimately formed alliances with the Nynee and Bear River peoples to prosecute an unsuccessful 1711 to 1713 war against North Carolina.

question.leadin: Answer these questions related to W. E. B. Du Bois.
question.text: The W. E. B. du Bois Institute for Afro-American Research is located on this university campus, which awarded him a Ph.D. degree in 1896.
question.clue: Harry Starr fought the Jewish quota in this institution, which merged with all-female Radcliffe College in 1977.

swap.leadin: This event was quashed after the rebels were spotted by a group of men traveling with William Bull, the state's Lieutenant Governor.
swap.text: Identify this rebellion organized by a man known as Jemmy.
swap.clue: During this event, participants marched toward Spanish Florida from South Carolina carrying a banner that read "Liberty!"

question.leadin: During this conflict, the Paxton Boys murdered twenty Susquehannocks at the Conestoga Massacre before being dispersed by Benjamin Franklin.
question.text: Name this 1763 war which included the Battle of Bloody Run. This war was named for an Ottawa leader who led the Siege of Fort Detroit.
question.answerHtml: Pontiac’s War [or Pontiac’s Rebellion, accept reasonable equivalents mentioning Pontiac]
question.clue: Anger at inadequate British defenses during this event led to the massacre of Conestogas by the Paxton Boys.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about religion in early America.
swap.text: The second one of these Christian revivals of religion was spearheaded by Charles Grandison Finney; the first by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitfield.
swap.clue: In 1801, over 20,000 people participated in one of these events by attending the Cane Ridge Revival in Kentucky.

question.text: After Edward Wingfield and John Ratcliffe were quickly dispatched, this man became president of the colony, and would soon after have his life saved by Pocahontas.
question.clue: This man was forced to return to England by a gunpowder injury, after negotiating a trade deal with native tribes to help alleviate the Starving Time.

swap.text: During the War of Jenkins' Ear, Oglethorpe led British troops against the Spanish in this battle fought in July 1742 on St. Simons Island. Its name refers to the high level of Spanish casualties that reportedly stained the location where this battle was fought.

question.leadin: This tribe was conned out of its land by the Penn family in the Walking Purchase.
question.text: Name this tribe that agreed to a 1682 treaty with William Penn. Peter Minuit (MIN-yoo-it) convinced members of this tribe to sell him Manhattan Island for some cheap glass beads.
question.clue: Along with the Mohicans, Christian members of what Native American tribe were massacred in the Gnadenhutten massacre?

swap.leadin: It began when the governor of the Dominion of New England left New York for Boston, leaving Francis Nicholson in charge. FTPE.
swap.text: Identify this 1689 to 1691 rebellion headed by a German trader and eventually put down by Henry Sloughter.
swap.clue: An attack by Canadians on Schenectady during this event helped its leader consolidate power.

question.leadin: The sachem ("SAY-chum") White Eyes negotiated a 1778 treaty named after this fort that allied the Lenape ("luh-NAH-pay") with the U.S.
question.text: Name this fort, which was the site of a siege during Pontiac's War where Henry Bouquet ("boo-KAY") employed smallpox blankets. This fort was built following the Forbes Expedition, during which nearby Fort Duquesne ("dew-KANE") was razed.
question.clue: One of the central events of the Rebellion was the siege of this fort, whose commander attempted to infect the Indians with smallpox. It was built near the site of the old Fort Duquesne in 1759.

swap.leadin: He was described as the "torchbearer of the revolution" in a book by Thomas Jefferson Wertenbacker, but that positive interpretation of his major action was opposed in a 1957 book by Wilcomb Washburn.
swap.text: Name this revolutionary leader, who defended his actions in a "Declaration of the People" issued at Middle Plantation.
swap.clue: This man called an Assembly to stamp out corruption and raise tobacco prices.

question.leadin: One of this man's expeditions was delayed for a month after fighting at Mauvila, and he was given some jewels at Cofitachequi. FTPE.
question.text: Name this explorer and one-time governor of Cuba who earlier served under Pedro Arias Davila. He was defeated at the Battle of Mabila.
question.clue: After he died of illness, his mission was continued by Luis de Moscoso Alvarado.

swap.text: As a teenager, Franklin published a series of letters in the New-England Courant using this feminine surname.
swap.clue: As an apprentice, Benjamin Franklin printed the New-England Courant newspaper, which featured this female persona of his giving humorous accounts of colonial life.
